display.title: Episode 169: The Rambam's Resting Place, Chapter 1 (Before Pesach)
display.summary_short: Ten days before Pesach, Uncle Yossi explains bedikas and mechiras chametz and eating matzah, then begins the life of the Rambam and the mystery of where he would be buried.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi's pre-Pesach show. He explains the preparations: cleaning out the chametz, searching for it on the night before Erev Pesach, selling the rest through the local rav, and the obligation to eat matzah on both Seder nights; helping Mommy and Tatty prepare earns Tzivos Hashem points, done with simchah. After a Pesach Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, story time turns to the Rambam, whose 850th birthday falls on this Erev Pesach. Uncle Yossi explains his name and the saying 'from Moshe to Moshe there arose none like Moshe'. A kindergarten boy leads the Shema. The story traces the Rambam's life: born in Cordoba, forced to flee persecution at fourteen, years of wandering, a storm at sea calmed by his prayer, a visit to the Kosel and the Me'aras HaMachpelah, and finally Egypt, where he wrote the Mishneh Torah, the Moreh Nevuchim and the Thirteen Principles of Faith. Before he passed away he asked to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron each claim the honor; next week brings the surprise. The show ends with birthday wishes, a half-price sale of Uncle Yossi's story records, and an invitation to a children's Siyum HaRambam on Chol HaMoed.
display.lesson: Prepare for Pesach properly and joyfully, and help your parents; the Rambam held on to Torah and mitzvos through years of wandering and hardship.

date.note: Pesach 'begins next Friday night'; Erev Pesach is Friday 5 April; bedikas chametz 'next Thursday night, the 4th of April'. Ep. 170 is the following Tuesday (2 April).

advisories.note: The young Rambam and his family flee cruel rulers who will not let Jews live by the Torah, and wander for years.
The Rambam's passing and his students' wish to bury him in Eretz Yisroel.
